The wilderness is Africa; we fled out of Jerusalem into Africa, the same place where Joseph took the young child and his mother. Then a place was prepared, which is the Americas. A thousand two hundred and threescore days: 1260 days, three and a half, the same period written as forty and two months and as a time, times, and the dividing of time in Daniel 7 and 8.

precepts.why:
“And their nobles shall be of themselves, and their governor shall proceed from the midst of them”. Our nobles are going to come from our own people. We are not going to have nobles of another race, like the mayor they have now in New York, Mamdani. That is not our people.

So the governor that proceeds from the midst of Israel is Christ, born in Bethlehem of Judah, ruling his people Israel. “I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me”, and then, “ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.”

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem”. East of Jerusalem is Babylon and the lands of the different captivities. Those wise men were Israel, living in the lands east of Jerusalem, “Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.”

The star they saw was a chariot, a light, what they call UFOs today, not a celestial body in the night sky. A planet cannot do what this did: “the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.” It guided them on the earth and stood over the house.

“And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother”. The house, not the manger. Christians show the wise men in a barn giving gifts to a baby, but time had passed; Christ was a young child now, a toddler of around two, walking and forming words. The wise men had been following that star at least two years. They were not three men; three is the number of the gifts, “gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.” They came as a caravan. With those gifts Christ was taken care of; he was not poor.

Herod, an Edomite who converted to being a Jew, a white man set up as king of Judea by Rome, “slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.” Thousands of black babies. That shows the child was around two when the wise men came. And when you see the synagogues of Satan killing babies in Palestine today, it does not surprise us; that is in their nature.

precepts.text: Out of Bethlehem shall come a Governor that shall rule the people Israel, which is Christ, the king the Most High set upon His holy hill.
precepts.point: Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion. Zion is another word for Israel, the term the Most High uses to refer to His people, and the king set upon the holy hill is Christ, set to be the ruler of His people Israel.

note.label: Psalm 2: Why Do the Heathen Rage

precepts.why:
“Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion.” Zion is another word for Israel, the term the Most High uses for His people, and the king set upon the holy hill is Christ. Matthew shows it: “And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.”

Out of Bethlehem comes a Governor that shall rule the people Israel. That Governor is Christ, the king the Most High set upon His holy hill, set to be the ruler of His people Israel. So even while the nations mock and oppress us and put us through all types of hell, He will have the last laugh, and His king is already set.

precepts.text: Out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.
precepts.point: My people is not a loose term in the scriptures. It is named.

note.label: Zechariah 8: I Will Return Unto Zion and Dwell in the Midst of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
They shall be my people, and I will be their God. My people is not a loose term in the scriptures; it is named. “And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.”

My people Israel. He is called the God of Israel because he is the God of that people and none else, and it is that people he saves from the east country and the west country to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem.

precepts.text: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents, and all kings shall fall down before him.
precepts.point: Wise men come from the east to Jerusalem to worship him. This is prophetic; it was written that kings from far off would come and bow before him.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
“there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem, Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.” This is prophetic; it was written that kings from far off would come and bow before him.

“The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents: the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts. Yea, all kings shall fall down before him: all nations shall serve him.” Kings from Tarshish, the isles, Sheba and Seba, far countries, bringing presents, offering gifts and falling down before him. The wise men from the east coming to worship the one born King of the Jews are the beginning of that psalm being fulfilled, and it ends with all kings falling down before him and all nations serving him.

precepts.text: The prophecy the priests were quoting: out of Bethlehem Ephratah shall he come forth that is to be ruler in Israel.
precepts.point: The same men who could quote where he would be born were blinded when he walked among them. Knowing the book is not the same as seeing the one the book speaks of.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
Herod “demanded of them where Christ should be born. And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judea: for thus it is written by the prophet”. The chief priests and scribes answered at once. They knew the scriptures concerning the messiah.

The prophet they quoted is Micah: “But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.” Out of Bethlehem Ephratah, little among the thousands of Judah, comes he that is to be ruler in Israel, the Governor “that shall rule my people Israel.” His goings forth are from of old, from everlasting. The priests had the verse; they could name the town before the child was found in it.

precepts.text: Israel obtained not that which he seeketh for, and the rest were blinded, and their table was made a snare and a trap unto them.
precepts.point: The same men who could quote where he would be born were blinded when he walked among them. Knowing the book is not the same as seeing the one the book speaks of.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
The same men who could quote where he would be born were blinded when he walked among them. Paul explains it: “Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded (According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear;) unto this day.”

Israel sought the messiah and did not obtain him; the election obtained it, and the rest were blinded, given the spirit of slumber and eyes that should not see. Then Paul brings David: “Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway.” Their table was made a snare and a trap unto them. The chief priests and scribes had the table set before them and it snared them: knowing the book is not the same as seeing the one the book speaks of.

precepts.text: The table David spoke of is the writing itself, noted in a book for the time to come.
precepts.point: The same men who could quote where he would be born were blinded when he walked among them. Knowing the book is not the same as seeing the one the book speaks of.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
What is the table that David said would be made a snare? Isaiah shows it: “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”. The table is the writing itself, noted in a book for the time to come.

So the table that became a snare and a trap to Israel was the scriptures. The chief priests and scribes had the writing before them; they could quote Micah on Bethlehem to Herod on demand, and that very table snared them. They were blinded to the ruler in Israel when he came out of Bethlehem as it was written. Knowing what is written in the book is not the same as seeing him.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
The angel tells Joseph, “Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.”

John saw this in the vision. A woman “being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered. And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.” And “the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born.” That is exactly what Herod set out to do: destroy the young child as soon as it was born. Herod, standing ready to devour the child, is the great red dragon before the woman.

precepts.text: That same dragon is called that old serpent, the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world.
precepts.point: They hid in Egypt among the Egyptians. A family that did not look like the people of that land would have been no more hidden there than anywhere else.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
The vision tells who the dragon is: “And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.” The great red dragon that stood before the woman to devour her child is that old serpent, the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world.

So behind Herod seeking the young child to destroy him is Satan himself, cast out into the earth with his angels. Herod's seeking was the dragon's seeking, and the flight into Egypt was a flight from the Devil.

Genesis gives that colour to a man: “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Esau came out red, which is the colour the dragon is given in the vision. The great red dragon that stood before the woman to devour her child carries the colour of Esau, and that is who the vision points to.

So the great red dragon standing before the woman to devour her child is men, moved by that old serpent, and in Matthew 2 the man standing to devour the child is Herod, seeking the young child to destroy him.

precepts.text: The prophecy quoted: when Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
precepts.point: They remain in Egypt until the death of Herod, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, Out of Egypt have I called my son.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
They stayed in Egypt until the death of Herod, “that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son.”

The prophet is Hosea: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.” When it was first spoken, the son called out of Egypt was Israel, when Israel was a child. Christ went down into Egypt and was called out of it as Israel was, and Matthew says that word was fulfilled in him. The son out of Egypt is Israel, and the son out of Egypt is Christ.

precepts.text: Pharaoh charged all his people to cast every son into the river, the same attempt to cut off a deliverer before he could grow.
precepts.point: Herod slays all the children in Bethlehem from two years old and under. This is the same pattern as Egypt, where the ruler killed the young children to stop a deliverer from rising.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
When Herod saw that he was mocked of the wise men, he “sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under”.

This is the same pattern as Egypt, where the ruler killed the young children to stop a deliverer from rising. “And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.” Pharaoh had every son cast into the river to cut off the deliverer before he could grow. Herod slew the children of Bethlehem two years old and under for the same reason, to cut off the child born King of the Jews before he could grow. The ruler changes; the attempt is the same.

precepts.text: Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they were not.
precepts.point: The mourning in Ramah was written of beforehand by Jeremiah.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
Matthew says the mourning in Rama was “that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet”, and here is where Jeremiah spoke it: “A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping; Rahel weeping for her children refused to be comforted for her children, because they were not.”

The weeping and great mourning for the children was written of beforehand. Rachel refusing to be comforted, because her children were not, is the very thing Matthew records being fulfilled. The prophet saw it long before it came to pass, and it fell out word for word.

precepts.text: Nathanael asks, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth, which shows how the place was regarded.
precepts.point: Nazareth had no reputation. That the messiah was raised there was itself a fulfilment of what the prophets spoke.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
When Herod was dead, Joseph brought the young child and his mother back into the land of Israel. But Archelaus reigned in Judea in the room of his father, so being warned of the Most High in a dream, Joseph turned aside into the parts of Galilee and dwelt in Nazareth, “that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.”

Nathanael shows how that place was regarded. When Philip tells him “We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph”, Nathanael answers, “Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?” Nazareth had no reputation; nobody expected anything good to come from there. Philip only says, “Come and see.”

That is the point of Matthew's words. The messiah was not raised in a city of renown, but in a place men looked down on, and that in itself was a fulfilment of what the prophets spoke.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

points: Herod slays all the children in Bethlehem from two years old and under. This is the same pattern as Egypt, where the ruler killed the young children to stop a deliverer from rising.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

points: After Herod dies the family returns, but Archelaus reigns in Judea, so being warned of the Most High Joseph turns aside into Galilee and dwells in Nazareth.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

points: Nazareth had no reputation. That the messiah was raised there was itself a fulfilment of what the prophets spoke.
